title: Generational gains in cognitive capacity and dementia incidence rates in Western countries
desc: The risk of developing dementia at any given age has fallen steadily in Europe and the United States over recent decades. A key unresolved question is whether recent generations reach older age with better cognitive capacity, experience slower cognitive decline, or both, as this has implications for when preventive interventions are likely to have the greatest impact. Analyzing ~783,000 episodic-memory assessments from ~219,000 individuals in five longitudinal studies followed for up to 30 years, we find that later-born generations benefit from a double dividend, with higher memory levels entering old age and slower decline thereafter. The combined advantage is large enough to plausibly account for the reported 13% per-decade decline in dementia incidence. Improvements are concentrated among the fastest decliners; later-born generations show longer periods of stable memory, and their slower decline is mirrored by lower rates of clinical impairment and slower hippocampal atrophy. Calendar-time trends affecting all generations simultaneously are unlikely to explain these differences. Because memory level is built mainly in early life whereas the rate of decline is shaped by conditions in adulthood, sustaining the decline in dementia incidence will require prevention policies that protect brain health across the whole lifespan, beginning in childhood.

title: Opportunistic Risk Assessment of Major Osteoporotic Fractures from Routine Chest Radiographs Using Deep Learning
Artificial intelligence-enabled clinical decision support: device regulation and decision influence.
source: PubMed · Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
desc: [Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA] Artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled clinical decision support (CDS) challenges core assumptions of the Food and Drug Administration's (FDA) recently updated CDS guidance, including the concepts of independent clinician review of outputs and manufacturer-intended use for exempting certain CDS tools from medical device regulation. We examine the FDA's January 2026 CDS guidance in the context of the evolving landscape of AI-enabled CDS tools, clinician interaction studies with AI-enabled CDS, and AI governance frameworks. Although the FDA's framework distinguishes non-device CDS from regulated software, AI-enabled CDS may synthesize and transform clinical information in ways that are difficult to verify during routine care, increasing clinician susceptibility to automation bias. Incorporating pragmatic triggers into existing governance frameworks can help identify scenarios with a heightened risk for clinical decision influence. Oversight calibrated to real-world clinical decision influence is needed to strengthen practical safety standards for AI-enabled CDS.

title: Interpretable AI links routine clinical gout phenotypes to multi-omic signatures and divergent health trajectories
desc: Integrative frameworks that connect scalable clinical phenotypes with molecular mechanisms are needed to resolve disease heterogeneity. We developed and externally evaluated an interpretable gout clinical-subset framework using routine data from 21,235 participants across UK Biobank (UKB; n = 10,599), the multicentre Chinese GoutRe registry (n = 8617), and MIMIC-IV (n = 2019). Unsupervised learning on six prespecified routine laboratory variables identified three subsets: C1, a low-burden state with preserved reserve; C2, a urate-metabolic inflammatory state with the greatest recurrence liability and a greater cardiometabolic and hepatic comorbidity burden; and C3, a state characterized by systemic vulnerability and higher mortality. In UKB, death-competing recurrence analysis showed a higher recurrence incidence for C2 versus C1 (subdistribution hazard ratio [sHR] 1.896, 95% CI 1.710–2.101), whereas C3 did not differ from C1 (sHR 0.994, 95% CI 0.887–1.112). A six-variable CRT model reconstructed the locked subset labels using nested 10-fold out-of-fold evaluation in UKB and external application without retraining in GoutRe and MIMIC-IV. One-versus-rest AUCs were 0.965/0.945/0.980 in UKB, 0.906/0.914/0.953 in GoutRe, and 0.912/0.898/0.962 in MIMIC-IV for C1/C2/C3, respectively. Genetic, proteomic, and metabolomic analyses supported distinct urate-inflammatory and systemic-vulnerability axes, although the C3 senescence-related genetic signal was nominal and requires replication. Routine laboratory data can identify gout clinical subsets with distinct molecular profiles and patterns of recurrence and mortality; whether these subsets can guide clinical management requires prospective evaluation.

title: Advancing computer-use agents for healthcare teams
Multimodal LLM for Breast Cancer Radiotherapy Target Auto-Contouring and Planning
desc: [Newly registered clinical trial, no results yet; sponsor: Xiaohui Zhao; conditions: Breast Cancer, Radiotherapy; type: OBSERVATIONAL; enrollment: 51000; status: NOT_YET_RECRUITING] Breast cancer remains the most prevalent malignancy among women worldwide, with a continuously increasing incidence. As a crucial component of comprehensive cancer treatment, radiotherapy plays a key role in reducing local recurrence rates and improving overall survival outcomes. However, traditional radiotherapy target volume contouring and treatment planning design rely heavily on clinician expertise, presenting challenges such as prolonged processing time, significant inter-observer variability, and high subjectivity in dose optimization. Although artificial intelligence has made substantial progress in automated contouring and planning, conventional single-modal models still face major limitations. These models struggle to effectively integrate clinical text, tumor biological characteristics, and dose distribution factors, resulting in restricted generalizability. Therefore, developing an intelligent radiotherapy assistance system capable of multimodal data fusion is of high clinical significance to enhance precision and efficiency in breast cancer radiotherapy. This study aims to develop an innovative breast cancer radiotherapy assistance system based on a multimodal large language model. By integrating multimodal imaging data (including CT, MRI, and ultrasound), pathology reports, and structured electronic health record text, the system realizes end-to-end intelligence from target volume contouring to treatment plan generation. Employing a multicenter, ambidirectional cohort design, the study collects comprehensive clinical data from breast cancer patients who have undergone breast-conserving surgery or mastectomy. Technologically, the system innovatively combines the natural language processing capabilities of large language models with the image analysis strengths of deep learning, utilizing attention mechanisms to achieve deep fusion and interactive comprehension of heterogeneous medical data. Notably, the system breaks through traditional radiotherapy planning workflows by jointly optimizing target contouring and dose planning as a unified pipeline, applying reinforcement learning algorithms to dynamically balance target volume coverage with organ-at-risk protection. The outcomes of this study will provide an important paradigm for the clinical application of AI in radiation oncology and advance the field of precision radiotherapy.

title: Clinician Acceptance of Large Language Model-Generated Discharge Summaries.
desc: [JAMA network open] Hospital discharge summaries are essential for continuity of care, but fragmented electronic health record (EHR) data can compromise their quality and safety. Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed for clinical documentation tasks despite limited evidence regarding their performance in health care settings compared with the current standard of care. To evaluate clinician acceptability of LLM-generated discharge summaries derived from EHRs compared with routine clinician-written summaries. In this retrospective comparative effectiveness study using a prespecified noninferiority framework, acceptability of LLM-generated discharge summaries was compared with clinician-authored discharge summaries. Admission records from 5 London hospitals for September 1, 2022, to September 30, 2023, were evaluated against the full admission record by practicing physicians. Admissions were eligible only if the clinician-authored discharge summary contained identifiable clinical summary, plan and requested actions, and information given sections. Data analysis was conducted from July 2025 to February 2026. LLM-generated summaries were produced using GPT-4o mini (July 18, 2024 release; OpenAI) and a clinician-codesigned prompt. The primary outcome was clinician signoff with no or minor edits, derived from 2 sequential questions: (1) whether the reviewer would sign the summary and (2) whether no, minor, or major edits were required. A 5-percentage-point noninferiority margin was prespecified. Secondary outcomes assessed accuracy, completeness, tone, and clarity (using a 5-point Likert scale: 1, poor; 2, fair; 3, good; 4, very good; and 5, excellent) and potential harmfulness of missing or incorrect information (using a 5-point Likert scale: 1, no harm; 2, minor harm; 3, moderate harm; 4, high harm; and 5, extremely high harm). The study sample included 1294 (649 clinician-authored and 645 LLM-generated) unique case discharge summaries that were evaluated against the full admission record by 12 practicing physicians. Case patients had a median age of 46.0 years (IQR, 26.2-69.8 years), 733 (56.6%) were assigned female at birth, and the median length of stay was 3.0 days (IQR, 1.0-7.0 days). title: Breath-Dx: A Time Series Classification Benchmark for Disease Screening with eNose
desc: Electronic nose (eNose) technology offers a portable, non-invasive route for disease screening via exhaled breath analysis. However, progress in the field is hindered by the lack of systematic benchmarks that compare machine learning methods under realistic conditions, particularly sensor drift, a known but rarely quantified failure mode. Most existing studies rely on small, private datasets with inconsistent protocols, rendering results non-comparable and slowing progress. We introduce Breath-Dx, the first comprehensive benchmark of time series classification methods for breath-based disease screening. Our work leverages the Scent of Health (S-OH) dataset, the largest public clinical eNose collection to date, comprising 1,234 patients across nine diagnostic groups, each providing a 17-channel multivariate time series with explicit temporal train/test splits that account for sensor drift. We systematically evaluate 10 methods spanning four families: feature-based tabular learners, convolution-based models, graph-based, and time series architectures. All methods degrade significantly under temporal validation (0.05-0.12 AUC drop compared to random cross-validation), confirming that drift embeds a strong temporal signal. Under this realistic evaluation, the best methods achieve ROC AUC of 0.74-0.76 for some lung conditions, though others remain near chance. Recurrent architectures show the most consistent performance across diseases, while specialized time series methods achieve the highest peak results. Demographic confounders matter: breath signals provide independent diagnostic value for some conditions but add little beyond age for others. We release the S-OH dataset, all temporal splits, evaluation protocols, and code to enable reproducible research and accelerate progress in clinical breathomics.

title: Uncovering the Invisible in Routine Radiology: Cross-Modal Detection of MRI-Verified Soft-Tissue Pathologies from CBCT via Physics-Guided 3D Self-Supervised Learning
desc: Routine X-ray modalities like cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) are optimized for high-contrast mineralized tissues, leaving soft-tissue abnormalities buried beneath photon noise and below human visual perception. Thus, detecting non-calcified pathologies requires secondary magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). We demonstrate that sub-visual radiographic signatures of soft-tissue pathology are physically preserved within routine CBCT scans and can be extracted for opportunistic screening using a targeted, physics-guided deep learning pipeline, even under extreme paired-data scarcity. Using the temporomandibular joint (TMJ) as a model system (N = 212 paired CBCT-MRI joints), we address the severe overfitting of high-capacity 3D networks through a two-stage framework. First, we employ a frozen full-grid 3D masked autoencoder (BertsWin) pre-trained on 6,550 unlabeled CBCT volumes via the GradientConductor (GCond) optimizer and an anatomy-aware objective (PhysLoss) redirecting gradient flow into the [-300, 300] HU soft-tissue window. Second, automated localization of the condylar zenith drives a deterministic 3D cropping that eliminates 81% of background osseous variance. Evaluated via a patient-isolated 3x10-fold stratified cross-validation protocol, a statistically robust sub-visual signal for MRI-verified synovial effusion (ROC AUC = 0.793) emerges exclusively from representations pre-trained with the PhysLoss and GCond regime. Crucially, only this setup captures true 3D anatomical chirality (p < 0.001) and high intra-patient structural consistency (0.791) over inter-patient noise; conversely, identical architectures pre-trained with standard L2 loss or unmasked variance decomposition (MVC) collapse to random guessing. These findings establish a generalizable paradigm for repurposing routine, low-contrast radiographic scans into opportunistic screening tools for occult soft-tissue disease.

title: Human-Agentic AI Collaboration Workflow for Trend Analysis of ChatGPT Applications in Healthcare
desc: Background: With the rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI), large language models (LLMs) such as ChatGPT have demonstrated strong potential to transform healthcare research and practice. However, LLMs are probabilistic and generate inherently variable outputs, which create risk and uncertainty in healthcare applications. Therefore, analyzing the current research landscape of ChatGPT applications is imperative to understand applied techniques and related concerns and to facilitate their practical integration into healthcare information systems. Objective: Leveraging LLM-based agentic AI with domain experts to analyze trends in ChatGPT healthcare applications and to examine the collaborative and interpretative capacities of LLM agents in broader contexts beyond narrowly defined topics. Methods: The review used a systematic search of the PubMed and Web of Science databases, following PRISMA-ScR guidelines, and focused on ChatGPT applications, associated concerns, applied techniques, and usage factors. To support the review process, an adaptive, iterative LLM-based agentic AI with a human-in-the-loop mechanism was employed for automated metadata extraction, identification, classification, and knowledge synthesis. The extracted information was subsequently used for temporal and thematic analyses, citation network construction, and main-path analysis. Results: Across 192 papers, the review identified 511 ChatGPT application types, 690 concern items, and 368 influence usage factors distinct from traditional IT, achieving a metadata error rate of 1.04%. The human-agentic AI workflow enabled efficient synthesis of contextual information across studies, addressing the growing challenge of timely evidence integration in medical knowledge. The findings provide insights into the evolving trajectories of ChatGPT applications in healthcare and demonstrate the value of an expert-validated human-agentic AI workflow in supporting literature analysis and streamlining review processes. Conclusion: This review provides a comprehensive overview of emerging ChatGPT applications, associated concerns, applied techniques, and usage factors in healthcare. The study further provides meaningful insights into the operational mechanisms of agentic AI, demonstrating the potential of human-AI collaboration for medical informatics research.

title: Automated segmentation of renal structures using brightfield images of unstained kidney biopsies
desc: The automated segmentation of unstained kidney brightfield microscopy images remains a significant challenge in medical imaging. In conventional histopathology, staining provides crucial structural and molecular contrast, allowing renal compartments and structures to be readily distinguished. The absence of staining markedly reduces this contrast, obscuring the fine architectural details that are essential for diagnosis. Addressing this gap would reduce reliance on staining protocols, reduce technical and interpretive variability, and preserve valuable tissue for downstream molecular or multi-omics analyses. Ultimately, automation of unstained image segmentation could enable faster, more objective tissue analysis while preserving samples for further molecular testing. In this work, we provide a comprehensive review of state-of-the-art segmentation methods applied to renal brightfield microscopy images. Current findings highlight a predominance of Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) based architectures for semantic segmentation approaches while recent trends point to the growing application of transformer-based and instance-segmentation strategies. However, the field is still hampered by the scarcity and poor annotation of publicly available renal datasets. Aiming to further contribute to the enhancement of the field, a dataset of 18 Whole Slide Images (WSIs) of unstained human kidney tissue is made publicly available. Additionally, in the dataset, we provide 543 annotated tiles extracted from the WSIs, facilitating further research into stain-independent segmentation approaches. As a third contribution, we present a preliminary case study, evaluating state-of-the-art deep learning segmentation architectures, including U-Net and Segment Anything Model (SAM). Our preliminary results indicate that deep learning models demonstrate promising segmentation performance in unstained kidney biopsies. In alignment with these findings, advanced customised loss functions and data augmentation were integrated into the supervised training of the promising U-Net, DeepLabv3+, and TransUNet models, achieving significant improvements compared to the baseline experiments. To exploit the abundance of unlabelled data, we further tested FixMatchSeg, a semi-supervised learning method; however, its segmentation performance remained slightly behind the supervised methods.
